newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Quarter of Hungary firms plan to invest - govt.
newsitem.headline: Quarter of Hungary firms plan to invest - govt.

text.p: A quarter of all Hungarian businesses plan to invest in the second half of the year and wish to employ a higher number of people, Labour Minister Peter Kiss said on Wednesday.

"One in four businesses plan to start a property or machinery investment in this period and plan to add further employees after an expansion in employment in the first half," he told a news conference.
Kiss released results of a survey made in March by Hungary's National Labour Centre among the managers of 4,611 businesses which employ 27.2 percent of employees.
The survey has been made twice a year for the following half year since September 1991, with the next one to be made in September.
He said the number of registered unemployed was 459,000 in June, or 10.3 percent, down from 10.6 percent or 472,821 registered unemployed in May.

"For the first time in almost 10 years employment is expanding in 1997," Kiss said. He added the ministry expected in 1997 the average number of registered unemployed closer to 450,000 than to 500,000.
